newsitem.title: USA: AT&T still sees PCS services in Q1 97 - CEO.
newsitem.headline: AT&T still sees PCS services in Q1 97 - CEO.

text.p: AT&T Corp chairman and CEO Robert Allen said that the telecommunications giant is still planning on starting to roll out its digital PCS services next year, as AT&T introduced new PCS-like wireless services on Wednesday.
Allen said that AT&T will offer PCS (personal communications services) based on the PCS frequencies AT&T purchased in the FCC auctions beginning in the first quarter of 1997.

"Don't get confused if you thought digital PCS won't be available until next year," Allen told a press conference. "It's the spectrum that won't be available," he said, referring to the frequencies AT&T will use for next generation wireless services.

Earlier, AT&T unveiled its newest wireless service, called AT&T Digital PCS, which will let customers consolidate voice, messaging and paging functions into one wireless telephone, using the comapny's currently available cellular frequencies.

Allen pointed out that customers do not care about the frequencies, whether they are cellular-based or PCS-based, and he said that AT&T plans to offer a wide array of wireless services under the name AT&T Digital PCS.
"Customers don't care about frequencies, they care about services," Allen said. The PCS services in 1997 will be the same as what was unveiled Wednesday, with a broader market reach.
"Those licenses will double our national footprint," Allen said, referring to the geographical area AT&T will be able to cover with the new frequencies.

AT&T executives declined to give any projections on how many new subscribers they hope to add with the Digital PCS. AT&T is targeting 70 million potential customers now, extending to more than 212 million potential users with the added frequencies.

AT&T said that the wireless phones to be used with this new service will cost from $150 and run up to $250, depending on the model. AT&T said that it will roll out new phones that access both digital and analog (used in cellular) frequencies next year.
